relationships.rationale: Publishing data assets as products requires each domain to have a single accountable owner responsible for the product.
Data products carry quality SLAs as part of their contract, which makes the producing team accountable for quality.
Discoverable, versioned data products require stable, machine-readable contracts so consumers can integrate without bespoke work.
Federating ownership to domain teams is the direct mandate for every data domain having a named, accountable steward.
Centralising standards while federating ownership depends on a single canonical definition per concept that all domain teams reference.
Self-service analytics depends on canonical, trusted definitions that consumers can rely on without re-deriving them.
Satisfying analytics use cases without bespoke pipeline work requires data products to expose open, machine-readable contracts.
This strategy is the direct mandate for classifying, consent-tracking, and access-controlling personal data from the point of capture.
Stream-first architectures for time-sensitive domains depend on producers taking responsibility for the quality of data the moment it is produced.
Real-time distribution often creates derived copies and materialised views, which must be explicit, expiring, and traceable to the canonical source.
End-to-end lineage depends on every derived value being traceable back to a single canonical definition rather than a parallel one.
Automated provenance metadata is what makes copies of canonical data explicit, expiring, and traceable to source, as this principle requires.
